answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, each identity locks its own refundable smart-contract bond, making multiple identities costly. Only when cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task can a slash occur. This approach ensures that no single entity can forge a majority vote, instead requiring a collective agreement to reach the zenith of consensus. As the dawn of decentralized governance breaks, this mechanism will become increasingly crucial in maintaining the integrity of blockchain systems.
